title: Sales Brief: Technical Rapid Reference & Negotiation Micro-Scripts (WIP)
content:
Purpose: one-page, portable reference for SEs/AE during discovery + negotiation. Focus: rapid technical rebuttals, compact PoC checklist, two-slide appendix for late-stage buyers. Status: working draft — intended to be clipped into SDR/AE playbooks and shared as a 1-pager PDF for field use.

Top-line framing (elevator):
- Position: Redwood gives predictable inference economics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments — tangible knobs (batching/cache/quant profiles) to trade latency for cost.
- Quick win to call out: we can often cut per-token cost by 20–60% vs naive hosted usage for customer workloads with caching + batching.

Quick objection/rebuttal snippets (speakable, <30s each):
- "Latency won't meet our SLA": 
  - Ask: what percentile and payload (tokens / prompt size)?
  - Snippet: "We map SLOs to routing policies — low-latency routes (pinned dedicated GPUs) or hosted fast-paths. For enterprise SLAs we offer Reserved Capacity with latency guarantees and automatic fallbacks so your tail latency is protected."
  - Proof point: cite internal SLA pages or customer case: "X corp saw 99.9th percentile drop from 1.1s→0.45s after pinning model variant."

- "Open-source models are lower quality / risky":
  - Snippet: "We surface vetted models and verify per-customer evals. For critical endpoints we recommend a validation set + rollback policy — Redwood can stage A/B of variants and maintain strict lineage so you can roll back instantly."

- "We can't share data / need on-prem":
  - Snippet: "Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) give you a local inference plane plus our control plane optionality; we integrate with KMS/HSM and provide audit logs. If required, we can run an air-gapped package with a professional services engagement."

Rapid qualification checklist (ask these in first technical call):
1) Expected conversational vs single-turn usage? (avg tokens in prompt + response)
2) Required p99/p95 latency targets and acceptable tail behavior
3) Compliance requirements: SOC2/PII/KMS/HSM/air-gap needed?
4) Traffic profile: peak qps and diurnal pattern; burstiness tolerance
5) Integration surface: function calling, streaming, embeddings, reranking?
6) Budget constraints / cost per 1M tokens target

Micro-PoC checklist (3–7 day quick validation pattern):
- Goal: validate latency, cost, and quality on representative workload.
- Minimal infra: 1 dedicated small node for latency target + hosted fallback.
- Steps:
  1. Customer provides 100–200 representative prompts (anonymized).
  2. Run baseline on hosted default model (capture tokens, latency).
  3. Enable prefix-KV caching and run same prompts; measure token reduction and latency shift.
  4. Try a quantized variant or lower-cost model to measure quality delta.
  5. Provide 1-slide summary: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens per call, unit cost delta, qualitative examples where outputs diverged.
- Success criteria: p95 within target AND quality drop <= agreed threshold on holdout prompts.

Two-slide technical appendix (copy-paste for decks):
- Slide A: Routing + Fallback matrix (rows: latency tiers, columns: capacity types — hosted/dedicated/private). Short bullets for when to pick each cell.
- Slide B: Cost optimization knobs (batch size, KV cache, quantization, model variant) with a one-line impact estimate: e.g., "KV cache: 15–40% token reduction for short conversations; batching: up to 2–3x throughput improvements at mild latency increase."

Negotiation micro-scripts (pricing concessions + commitment asks):
- Common concession: "We need better unit price"
  - Script: "We can deliver a unit discount tied to Reserved Capacity commit (3/6/12 mo). Start with a small baseline commit to enable predictable scheduling and we’ll include an Optimization workshop to identify immediate cost wins."
- Common concession: "We need a trial with production traffic"
  - Script: "We offer a staged reserved pool with preconfigured fallbacks. For trials we recommend a quota-limited dedicated pool plus an operational runbook so we can observe cost & tail-latency before scaling."

Field play: when to push Dedicated vs Hosted quick guide (decision heuristics):
- Push Dedicated when: sustained QPS that exceeds shared-hosted predictability, customer requires p99 SLAs, or data isolation/compliance needs are strict.
- Push Hosted when: exploring use cases, highly variable workloads, or when customer wants lowest time-to-value.
- Push Private when: legal/regulatory constraint or air-gap/secret models required.

Conversation snippets for platform engineers (technical depth):
- On batch sizing: "Batching trades latency for higher throughput; our runtime can do continuous batching with adaptive thresholds per route so you get batching benefits with controlled tail impact."
- On KV caching: "We expose prefix-based KV cache and sticky routing to preserve cache locality; typical conversation flows can see a large token reduction when prompts reuse context."
- On quantization: "We support multiple quant profiles and auto-suggest profiles based on per-workload eval. For retrieval-heavy patterns a 4-bit profile often hits the best cost/quality sweet spot."

Open questions / follow-ups (notes to self):
- Need canonical p95/p99 latency reduction numbers for the most common model families — ask Research for a short table.
- Template PoC contract language for 30-day reserved pilots — coordinate with RevOps.
- Add 2–3 one-paragraph competitor rebuttals (GCP AI, vendor X) with specific differentiators (e.g., unified routing, fallback policies).

Examples: email templates and quick links (paste these into AE sequences):
- Subject: Quick 10-min proof we can hit your p95 target
  - Body: "Hi <Name>, can you share a small sample of representative prompts? We’ll run a 48-hour micro-PoC and share a one-slide summary detailing latency and unit-cost delta. No infra to provision on your side for the first pass."

- Subject: Reserve capacity option — simplified starter offer
  - Body: "Hi <Name>, for predictable latency and lower unit costs we can provision a starter reserved pool for X/month with a 60-day evaluation and rollback clauses. I’ll attach the simple term sheet if you want to iterate."

Appendix: quick links and resources (internal):
- PoC template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ENG-POC-templates
- SLA & Dedicated docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SLA-Dedicated
- Research: ticket JIRA-3127 for latency benchmark results
- Slack: #g2m-field-ops (pin: "PoC quick checklist")

Last notes (informal):
- Keep this file intentionally compact; make a 1-page PDF for sales kit and a 2-slide appendix for deck insertion.
- Want a short recorded demo (3–4 min) that shows switching routing policy in Console + seeing p95 drop — ask Product for a recording.

Unresolved: how best to surface model-variant A/B results in Console screenshots for sales decks. Current mockups are noisy; need a cleaned 2-panel screenshot.
